text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — the new kernel-selector change landed in staging an hour ago. I'm seeing a weird per-token tail for ~6 tenants. Opening this thread for profiler outputs + dashboard asks.

Samir Patel: Can you paste the perf profile or a quick p95/p99 snapshot? Is this across all routes or specific models?

Maria Chen: Most visible on chat-route `/v1/chat` and a couple of high-concurrency embedding routes. Token-latency breakdown shows scheduler+kernel on the critical path. p95 token latency jumped from 12ms -> 28ms for some workspaces.

Jia Li: Dropping the sampling flame snippet I grabbed from perf-tools. Looks like kernel_dispatch spends more time when `batched_seq_len < 32` which matches small prompt workloads from test orgs.

Jia Li: ```
# simplified flame:
kernel_dispatch 68%
kv_lookup 9%
batching_wait 11%
serialize 6%
network 6%
```

Samir Patel: Interesting. Could batching heuristics be misclassifying small requests into a low-throughput path that triggers a slower kernel?

Kai Novak: That aligns with our kernel-selection rule: if estimated batch tokens < threshold we pick kernel-v1 (low-mem conservative) else kernel-v2 (vectorized). New selector added a micro-penalty for switching; might be misestimating for multi-tenant mixes.

Anita Gomez: From an observability perspective, we need token-level breakdowns per-route and per-workspace. Right now Grafana panels are only per-model. Ops wants RBAC so customer success can view their own workspace KPIs without seeing other orgs.

Maria Chen: For quick triage, I posted a PromQL query I'm using in staging:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, kernel, workspace_id))
```
But workspace_id cardinality is scary in prod.

Samir Patel: Agree on cardinality. Two-tier approach: (1) high-card workspace label only on aggregated counters (sampled) and (2) coarse per-workspace rollups exported periodically. That keeps `token_latency_*` low-card.

Jia Li: Also add route-level KPIs: `route_token_p50/p95/p99`, `route_qps`, `route_cache_hit_rate`. For KV cache behavior add `kv_lookup_ms` with `cache_hit` boolean label.

Kai Novak: Implementation notes: We can add `workspace_scope` as a low-card tag (e.g., `workspace_scope=paid|trial|partner`) for most dashboards, and only attach `workspace_id` to a high-card sampled metric `workspace_token_latency_sample` with 1% sampling. That will let account teams pull their own detailed view.

Anita Gomez: For RBAC, the console needs per-dashboard templating with a workspace variable that checks session permissions. Suggest we add an API endpoint that lists dashboards viewable by a token (uses RBAC), and Grafana uses proxy auth.

Maria Chen: Back to perf regression — Jia, can you run a microbenchmark to replay small random-combined requests and toggle kernel selector? Maybe a quick ab test: kernel-selector=old vs kernel-selector=new.

Jia Li: Running it now. Early result: 10k requests, 95th token latency old=13ms new=25ms on tenant A (heavy small-requests mix). Kernel-level traces show repeated kernel fallback on first tokens, causing extra serialization.

Samir Patel: That fallback is the issue. We added a safety fallback path when an optimized kernel reports a mismatch; but the backoff/retry cost is too high. Options: reduce fallback cost (inline path) or improve selector accuracy so fallback rarely triggers.

Kai Novak: I'll open two PRs: one to tighten selector heuristics (predict next-token distribution based on recent N requests per-queue), and one to add a fast inline fallback that bypasses heavy traces.

Anita Gomez: Dashboard work: I'll create a new folder `Per-Workspace KPIs` in Grafana with panels: p50/p95/p99 token latency, cache hit rate, QPS, error rate, and kernel-fallback-rate. Panels should accept `workspace_id` template and enforce RBAC.

Maria Chen: Action items: Kai (selector fixes + fast-fallback) / Jia (microbench + perf traces) / Anita (workspace dashboards + RBAC proxy). Samir and I will coordinate on rollout plan and sample rate for workspace metrics.

deploy-bot: deploy #canary-kernel-selector to `staging` succeeded (build 86f3c9). Monitoring policies: notify on route_token_p95 > 20ms for 3 consecutive windows. :white_check_mark:

Samir Patel: After Kai's PR, let's run a canary split 10% of tenants with the new selector and compare per-route KPIs over 6 hours. If fallback_rate > 0.5% revert.

Jia Li: Uploaded perf traces to the shared S3: s3://redwood-staging/profiler/1769123456/ — contains flamegraphs, pprof and a small script to repro.

Maria Chen: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread open for updates. If you push any selectors to prod, ping here and tag `@oncall` so the alert window is widened during rollout.

Kai Novak: PRs linked: #4523 (selector heuristics), #4524 (inline-fast-fallback). ETA EOD.

Anita Gomez: Dashboard draft link: https://grafana.internal/d/tenant-kpis/dash-tenant-kpis (read-only until RBAC proxy wired).

Maria Chen: Great. Will reconvene after the 6hr canary. :rocket:
